children: India's stronger-than-expected GDP growth print underscores the resilience of domestic demand, prompting DBS to raise its FY 2027 growth forecast to 7.3% from 6.8%. Consumption, public investment and manufacturing provide a solid base despite external shocks, economist Radhika Rao says in a note. The data also gives the central bank room to tighten policy if inflation risks persist, she says. Risks to the outlook now stem less from domestic weakness and more from elevated oil prices, rupee depreciation, monsoon conditions and tighter global financial conditions. (jihye.lee@wsj.com)
